title: Irregular benchmarks OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber on offensive-security suites
summary: Irregular, working with OpenAI, reported GPT-6 Cyber solving every multi-stage scenario and atomic challenge at least once while breaching no hardened target on FrontierCyber, the most severe item at medium. METR published an assessment of AI R&D acceleration at Anthropic, about 1.9x on benchmarks, and a review of Anthropic's August Risk Report. Epoch AI moved its Capabilities Index to a Bayesian model. No critical or high item was found, but advisory and incident coverage was weak.

items.title: Irregular benchmarks OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber: every multi-stage and atomic challenge solved at least once
items.summary: Irregular, working with OpenAI, ran GPT-6 Cyber on its offensive-security suites. On FrontierCyber (real systems) it solved 90 of 288 challenges versus 96 for GPT-6 Astra, none of the 15 hardest, and breached no hardened targets. It completed 11 of 11 CyScenarioBench scenarios at least once (Astra: 8 of 11) and all 22 Atomic Challenges at least once. Irregular says the lower FrontierCyber count alone does not show a regression.
items.note: Vendor-commissioned evaluation (done with OpenAI); Astra figures differ from its original system card because both were rerun on updated challenge sets.

items.title: METR assesses AI R&D acceleration at Anthropic at roughly 1.9x on benchmarks
items.summary: After an eleven-week high-access evaluation at Anthropic (Aug 12 to Oct 29, 2026), METR estimates that growth on Anthropic's internal capability index since October 2025 runs about 1.9x the historical rate (95% CI 1.5 to 2.8x). It judges AI to be the likely main driver, finds no convincing bottlenecks over the next 12 months with low confidence, and notes Anthropic redacted much of the most informative evidence, so the report leans on METR's judgment.
items.products: Anthropic internal frontier models (AI R&D acceleration)
items.note: Only the first ~100k characters of this long page were read; figures are as METR states them.

items.title: METR reviews the automated-R&D section of Anthropic's August 2026 Risk Report
items.summary: METR agrees with Anthropic that models as of July 15 posed low risk of automating R&D or causing acute catastrophic risk, but calls the public report's conclusion on the 2x acceleration threshold overconfident and says that threshold may plausibly have been crossed. It argues the public report understated leading-indicator acceleration and uncertainty relative to the private report, and cannot rule out substantial further acceleration within six months.
items.products: Anthropic Risk Report (August 2026), automated R&D section

items.title: Epoch AI moves its Capabilities Index to a Bayesian model
items.summary: Epoch replaced the least-squares and bootstrap fitting of the Epoch Capabilities Index with a Bayesian model giving credible intervals and direct probability comparisons between models, with per-benchmark noise levels. Across 252 models, Epoch reports new intervals about 13% narrower for models at or above ECI 125, out-of-sample 90% interval coverage of 89.6% versus 84.2% before, and slightly steeper frontier trends.
